   587→    def build_gui_context(
   588→        self,
   589→        context: dict[str, str],
   590→        project_overrides: dict[str, str],
   591→    ) -> dict[str, str]:
   592→        """Build context specific to the GUI toolkit."""
   593→        bootstraps = get_gui_bootstraps()
   594→        bootstrap_options = self._gui_bootstrap_choices(bootstraps)
   595→
   596→        # Map the override value to the annotated override value so we can use it with self.select_option
   597→        # If a user specifies the override value PySide6, then we want it to be mapped to the annotated value
   598→        # "PySide6       (does not support iOS/Android deployment)"
   599→        # since that is the option presented to the user. To accomplish this, we map the bootstrap classes
   600→        # to their annotated names and do a reverse lookup from the override bootstrap class to the annotated name.
   601→        #
   602→        # We do it this way to ensure consistent prompting for the user.
   603→        if bootstrap_override := project_overrides.pop("bootstrap", None):
   604→            reverse_lookup = {v: k for k, v in bootstrap_options.items()}
   605→            if self.validate_selection_override(bootstraps.keys(), bootstrap_override):
   606→                bootstrap_override = reverse_lookup[bootstraps[bootstrap_override]]
   607→
   608→        selected_bootstrap = self.select_option(
   609→            intro=(
   610→                "What GUI toolkit do you want to use for this project?\n"
   611→                "\n"
   612→                "Additional GUI bootstraps are available; visit "
   613→                "https://beeware.org/bee/briefcase-bootstraps "
   614→                "for a full list of known GUI bootstraps."
   615→            ),
   616→            variable="GUI Framework",
   617→            default=None,
   618            options=bootstrap_options.keys(),
   619→            override_value=bootstrap_override,
   620→        )
   621→        bootstrap_class = bootstrap_options[selected_bootstrap]
   622→
   623→        gui_context = {}
   624→
   625→        if bootstrap_class is not None:
   626→            bootstrap: BaseGuiBootstrap = bootstrap_class(context=context)
   627→
   628→            # Iterate over the Bootstrap interface to build the context.
   629→            # Returning ``None`` is a special case that means the field should not be
   630→            # included in the context and instead deferred to the template default.
   631→
   632→            if hasattr(bootstrap, "extra_context"):

   642→    def _gui_bootstrap_choices(self, bootstraps):
   643→        """Construct the list of available GUI bootstraps to display to the user."""
   644→        # Sort the options alphabetically first
   645→        ordered = OrderedDict(sorted(bootstraps.items()))
   646→
   647→        # Ensure the first 5 options are: Toga, PySide6, Pygame
   648→        ordered.move_to_end("Pygame", last=False)
   649→        ordered.move_to_end("PySide6", last=False)
   650→        ordered.move_to_end("Toga", last=False)
   651→
   652→        # Option None should always be last
   653→        ordered["None"] = None
   654→        ordered.move_to_end("None")
   655→
   656→        # Construct the bootstrap options as they should be presented to users.
   657→        # The name of the bootstrap is its registered entry point name. Along with the
   658→        # bootstrap's name, a short message important to a user's choice can be shown
   659→        # also; for instance, several show "does not support iOS/Android deployment".
   660→        bootstrap_choices = {}
   661→        max_len = max(map(len, ordered))
   662→        for name, klass in ordered.items():
   663→            if annotation := getattr(klass, "display_name_annotation", ""):
   664→                annotation = f"{' ' * (max_len - len(name))} ({annotation})"
   665→            bootstrap_choices[f"{name}{annotation or ''}"] = klass
   666→
   667→        return bootstrap_choices

   200→        BRIEFCASE_HOME environment variable. If that isn't defined, use a platform-
   201→        specific default data path.

   203→        if data_path is None:
   204→            try:
   205→                briefcase_home = os.environ["BRIEFCASE_HOME"]
   206→                data_path = Path(briefcase_home).resolve()
   207→                # Path("") converts to ".", so check for that edge case.
   208→                if briefcase_home == "" or not data_path.is_dir():
   209→                    raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   210→                        "The path specified by BRIEFCASE_HOME does not exist."
   211→                    )
   212→            except KeyError:
   213→                if platform.system() == "Darwin":  # pragma: no-cover-if-not-macos
   214→                    # macOS uses a bundle name, rather than just the app name
   215→                    app_name = "org.beeware.briefcase"
   216→                else:  # pragma: no-cover-if-is-macos
   217→                    app_name = "briefcase"
   218→
   219→                data_path = PlatformDirs(
   220→                    appname=app_name,
   221→                    appauthor="BeeWare",
   222→                ).user_cache_path

   228→                f"""

   230→

   232→

   234→you from building and packaging applications.

   237→a custom location for Briefcase's tools.
   238→

   245→                # interactions within %LOCALAPPDATA% to a sandboxed location.

   247→                # performed via ``cmd.exe`` in a different process. Once this
   248→                # directory exists in the "real" %LOCALAPPDATA%, Windows will
   249→                # allow normal interactions without attempting to sandbox them.
   250→                if platform.system() == "Windows":  # pragma: no-cover-if-not-windows
   251→                    subprocess.run(
   252→                        ["mkdir", data_path],
   253→                        shell=True,
   254→                        check=True,
   255→                        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
   256→                        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
   257→                    )
   258→                else:  # pragma: no-cover-if-is-windows

   260→            except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, OSError):
   261→                raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   262→                    f"""
   263→Failed to create the Briefcase directory to store tools and support files:
   264→
   265→    {data_path}
   266→
   267→You can set the environment variable BRIEFCASE_HOME to specify
   268→a custom location for Briefcase's tools.
   269→
   270→"""
   271→                )
   272→

   701→    def parse_options(self, extra):
   702→        """Parse the command line arguments for the Command.
   703→
   704→        After the initial ArgumentParser runs to choose the Command for the selected
   705→        platform and format, a new ArgumentParser is created here to parse the remaining
   706→        command line arguments specific to the Command. Additionally, the default
   707→        options for disabling input, log verbosity, and log saving are parsed out and
   708→        saved to the Command.
   709→

   711→            ArgumentParser runs over the command line.
   712→        :return: dictionary of parsed arguments for Command, and a dictionary of parsed
   713→            configuration overrides.
   714→        """
   715→        default_format = getattr(
   716→            get_platforms().get(self.platform), "DEFAULT_OUTPUT_FORMAT", None
   717→        )
   718→        # only show supported formats for Commands that support formats
   719→        if default_format is not None and self.command not in {"new", "dev", "upgrade"}:
   720→            formats = list(get_output_formats(self.platform).keys())
   721→            formats[formats.index(default_format)] = f"{default_format} (default)"
   722→            supported_formats_helptext = (
   723→                f"Supported formats:\n  {', '.join(sorted(formats, key=str.lower))}"
   724→            )
   725→        else:
   726→            supported_formats_helptext = ""
   727→
   728→        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   729→            prog=self.cmd_line.format(
   730→                command=self.command,
   731→                platform=self.platform,
   732→                output_format=self.output_format,
   733→            ),
   734→            description=self.input.textwrap(
   735→                f"{self.description}\n\n{supported_formats_helptext}"
   736→            ),
   737→            formatter_class=(
   738→                lambda prog: RawDescriptionHelpFormatter(prog, width=MAX_TEXT_WIDTH)
   739→            ),
   740→        )
   741→
   742→        self.add_default_options(parser)
   743→        self.add_options(parser)
   744→
   745→        # If the command allows passthrough arguments, add an option for the help,
   746→        # then process the argument list to strip out the passthrough args.
   747→        if self.allows_passthrough:
   748→            parser.add_argument(
   749→                "--",
   750→                dest="passthrough",
   751→                metavar="ARGS ...",
   752→                required=False,
   753→                help="Arguments to pass to the app",
   754→            )
   755→            args, passthrough = split_passthrough(extra)
   756→        else:
   757→            args = extra
   758→
   759→        # Parse the full set of command line options from the content
   760→        # remaining after the basic command/platform/output format
   761→        # has been extracted.
   762→        options = vars(parser.parse_args(args))
   763→
   764→        if self.allows_passthrough:
   765→            options["passthrough"] = passthrough
   766→
   767→        # Extract the base default options onto the command
   768→        self.input.enabled = options.pop("input_enabled")
   769→        self.logger.verbosity = options.pop("verbosity")
   770→        self.logger.save_log = options.pop("save_log")
   771→
   772→        # Parse the configuration overrides
   773→        overrides = parse_config_overrides(options.pop("config_overrides"))
   774→
   775→        return options, overrides
